title: Bratwurst with Quick Sauerkraut
subtitle: Pork sausages with tangy quick-pickled cabbage
excerpt: Homemade pork sausages pan-fried until golden, served with a quick sauerkraut made from shredded cabbage and vinegar. This version uses fennel seeds in place of caraway, which are not currently in the pantry list but give a similar anise-scented result.
sourceNotes: Bratwurst is one of Germany's most well-known sausages, with regional variations across the country dating back to the 14th century. Sauerkraut has been a staple preservation technique across Central and Eastern Europe for centuries, used to extend the shelf life of cabbage through winter.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The quick sauerkraut improves if left to sit for 30 minutes before serving.

content.text: This recipe uses fennel seeds as a substitute for caraway seeds, which are not available in the pantry list. Fennel gives a slightly sweeter, anise-like flavour that works well with both the sausages and the cabbage.

items.prepNote: lightly crushed, divided between sausages and sauerkraut

content.text: Mix the pork mince with half the fennel seeds and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Shape firmly into 4 sausages. Chill for 10 minutes while you prepare the sauerkraut.

Put the shredded cabbage, onion, carrot, remaining fennel seeds, and a generous pinch of salt in a large bowl. Toss well, then massage with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the cabbage starts to soften and release juice. Stir in the vinegar. Leave to sit while the sausages cook.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the sausages and fry, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through and browned on all sides. Cut one open to check there is no pink in the centre.
Taste the sauerkraut and adjust seasoning. Serve the sausages alongside the sauerkraut with Dijon mustard on the side.

items.fix: Cook on medium heat and turn them gently.

items.cause: Too much vinegar or not enough salt
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar or a little more salt to balance it.
Massage longer until cabbage feels soft and wet.
